title: Great Chinese Famine
summary: A famine in China, dated by Smil from spring 1959 to the end of 1961, followed the Great Leap Forward. Death estimates vary: American demographers first put it at 16.5 to 23 million, later studies at 23 to 30 million, and Carnegie Council cites an official figure of 15 million. Smil calls it largely man-made; Carnegie notes authorities blamed drought and Soviet debt.

uncertainty.note: Sources give roughly 1959-1961; the Carnegie Council article places the official "Three Years of Natural Disasters" at 1960-62.

as_recorded.value: between the spring of 1959 and the end of 1961 some 30 million Chinese starved to death

importance.justification: Described by Smil as the largest famine in human history, with deaths estimated in the tens of millions.

audience_note: This record concerns mass starvation. Death tolls are disputed and range widely by estimate, and interpretations of responsibility differ between scholars and official accounts. Figures here are attributed to their authors.
